action.action-desc: Mr. Carter of Georgia (for himself, Mr. Cárdenas, Mr. Graves of Georgia, and Mr. Bishop of Georgia) introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce

form.official-title: To amend title XIX of the Social Security Act to provide for the continuing requirement of Medicaid coverage of nonemergency transportation to medically necessary services.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Protecting Patients Transportation to Care Act.

section.header: Continuing requirement of medicaid coverage of nonemergency transportation to medically necessary services

subsection.text: Section 1902(a)(10) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1396a(a)(10)) is amended—

paragraph.text: in subparagraph (A), in the matter preceding clause (i), by striking and (21) and inserting , (21), and (30); and
in subparagraph (C)(iv), by striking and (17) and inserting , (17), and (30).

subsection.text: Section 1905 of such Act (42 U.S.C. 1396d) is amended—

subparagraph.text: in paragraph (29), by striking and at the end;
by redesignating paragraph (30) as paragraph (31) and by striking the comma at the end and inserting a semicolon; and
by inserting after paragraph (29) the following new paragraph:

paragraph.text: subject to subsection (ff), nonemergency transportation to medically necessary services, consistent with the requirement of section 431.53 of title 42, Code of Federal Regulations, as in effect as of June 1, 2019; and
by adding at the end the following new subsection:

subsection.header: Nonemergency transportation to medically necessary services

paragraph.text: Notwithstanding any other provision of this title, to be eligible for federal financial participation under this title for expenses incurred as medical assistance or as an administrative expense for nonemergency transportation to medically necessary services described in subsection (a)(30), the State Medicaid agency of such State must have in place a prior authorization or utilization management requirement for such services.

For purposes of paragraph (1), the term prior authorization means a process through which a request for provisional affirmation of coverage is submitted for review before the service involved is furnished and before a claim is submitted for payment for such service.

subsection.text: The amendments made by this section shall take effect on the date of the enactment of this Act and shall apply to transportation on or after such date.
